blocks.content: By default, the flat network model covered earlier in this module means every Pod can reach every other Pod, with no restriction at all, a NetworkPolicy is how you actually restrict that, a firewall for Pod-to-Pod traffic.

Without any NetworkPolicy at all, the flat network model from the Pod-to-Pod Communication topic means literally every Pod can reach every other Pod in the cluster, no restriction whatsoever, by default.

blocks.alt: No restriction at all, by default, a genuinely open network

blocks.content: A NetworkPolicy object defines rules restricting which Pods can talk to which others, functioning conceptually just like a firewall, but expressed in terms of Kubernetes label selectors rather than raw IP ranges.

blocks.alt: A firewall, expressed in terms of labels and selectors instead of raw IPs

blocks.content:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: backend-allow-frontend
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: frontend

blocks.content: A common real pattern restricts a backend service to only accept traffic from frontend Pods specifically, blocking every other Pod in the cluster from reaching it directly, exactly the shape of the manifest above.

blocks.alt: Only the intended caller allowed through, everything else explicitly blocked

blocks.content: A NetworkPolicy can control both directions independently, ingress rules restrict incoming traffic to matching Pods, egress rules restrict outgoing traffic from them, letting you control both what can reach a Pod and what it is allowed to reach.

blocks.alt: Both directions controllable independently, incoming and outgoing traffic alike

blocks.content: 5. The Important Caveat: CNI Support Required
blocks.text: 5. The Important Caveat: CNI Support Required

blocks.content: This is genuinely worth knowing before relying on it: a NetworkPolicy object is just a declaration, it only actually takes effect if the cluster's CNI plugin, covered in the previous topic, supports enforcing it, not every CNI plugin does, some flat-network implementations simply ignore NetworkPolicy objects entirely.

blocks.alt: A declared rule that silently does nothing without genuine CNI-level enforcement

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Without a NetworkPolicy, every Pod can reach every other Pod by default, NetworkPolicy adds firewall-like rules restricting that, using label selectors, not raw IPs.
Enforcement genuinely depends on the CNI plugin actually supporting it, worth verifying explicitly, a NetworkPolicy on an unsupported CNI silently does nothing.
